record.title: Sage-A1.5 tests learned orchestration and verification in a 35B open-weight agent model
record.summary: Shanghai AI Laboratory describes Sage-A1.5 as a Mixture-of-Experts agent model with 35B total and 3B active parameters whose paper describes learned task orchestration and iterative evidence checking for long-horizon work. The authors report that enabling orchestration raises BrowseComp from 81.7 to 82.8 and DeepResearch-Bench II from 43.7 to 47.5, while broader comparisons are mixed. Model weights are available under Apache-2.0. The results are author-reported, and independent reproduction, external deployment performance, and total inference cost remain open. In one scientist-guided computational-chemistry workflow, the authors report about 12 hours of agent execution versus an estimated human work-week; that human-time estimate is not a matched measurement. The paper depicts quantized local deployment, but reports no matched hardware speed or cost result.

claims.label: DEMONSTRATED
claims.text: Shanghai AI Laboratory’s Oct. 20 arXiv report introduces Sage-A1.5 as a 35B-parameter Mixture-of-Experts agent model trained for task orchestration and iterative evidence checking; its weights are publicly available under Apache-2.0.

claims.label: CLAIMED
claims.text: In the paper’s author-run ablation, enabling Sage-A1.5 orchestration changes BrowseComp from 81.7 to 82.8 and DeepResearch-Bench II from 43.7 to 47.5; the paper reports the teacher configuration at 81.6 and 53.6 respectively.

claims.label: CLAIMED
claims.text: The paper’s broader comparison table shows mixed results: Sage-A1.5 leads the listed larger models on some measures such as FrontierScience-Olympiad and IFBench, while trailing them on several coding, machine-learning, and research-report benchmarks.

claims.label: CLAIMED
claims.text: A preliminary pVisor static test reported about 80% lower resident memory after offload than its running baseline in one run per condition; the paper says savings depend on workload and management/restoration overhead.

claims.label: NOT_ESTABLISHED
claims.text: The paper and model card do not establish independent replication, robust generalization to external deployments, or a net inference-cost advantage after subagent compute and runtime overhead.

claims.label: CLAIMED
claims.text: In one scientist-guided computational-chemistry workflow, the authors report about 12 hours of agent execution and estimate that a human researcher implementing the same workflow from scratch would need about one work-week; the human-time comparison is an estimate, not a measured matched benchmark.

claims.label: CLAIMED
claims.text: The paper depicts local quantized Sage-A1.5 variants as a 35B-total, 3B-active-parameter Mixture-of-Experts model and describes deployment across heterogeneous local hardware; it reports no hardware-matched throughput, quality or cost comparison for these configurations.

evidence_gaps.description: The benchmark results and orchestration ablation are author-reported; an independent reproduction under a pinned harness and matched compute has not been located.
The paper does not provide a matched end-to-end inference-cost comparison accounting for parallel subagents, token usage, latency and runtime overhead.
The approximately 80% resident-memory result is a preliminary static test with one run per condition; workload sensitivity and restoration costs remain unmeasured.

The model-card GitHub link resolves to the earlier Agents-A1 repository; the inspected repository does not identify Sage-A1.5 training or evaluation code. This does not establish that no A1.5-specific code is available elsewhere.

The paper’s case studies are author-selected workflow demonstrations; no independent review of their artifacts or measured human-versus-agent quality, labor, or cost comparison was identified. The ~12-hour versus estimated one-week chemistry comparison is an author estimate.

brief.importance_rationale: If sustained, reported gains from training an open 35B model to delegate parallel work and revise its approach could influence the cost and design of long-horizon research agents. Open weights improve inspectability and access, but author-run mixed benchmark results do not establish a dependable capability or cost advantage.
limitations: All performance comparisons in the report are author-reported; no independent reproduction was identified.
The orchestration ablation gains are benchmark-specific and do not establish improved capability across all long-horizon tasks.
The comparison table is mixed, with Sage-A1.5 trailing larger models on several coding, ML engineering, deep-research and scientific measures.
The preliminary pVisor memory result uses one run per condition and cannot establish general savings or improved inference economics.
The model card’s linked GitHub repository is for the earlier Agents-A1 model; an A1.5-specific training/evaluation implementation was not identified at that destination.

The paper’s scientific case studies are author-selected demonstrations: the neuroscience task reanalyzes existing data using another framework, chemistry is scientist-guided, and some analyses use simulated or synthetic inputs. They do not establish autonomous discovery of new scientific results. The ~12-hour agent versus estimated human work-week comparison is not a measured matched productivity study.

The paper’s 35B-total/3B-active parameter description and heterogeneous local-deployment claims do not establish memory requirements, hardware compatibility, throughput or cost under a matched workload.

technical.claimed_result: The authors report that Sage-A1.5 combines learned subagent orchestration with iterative verification and achieves benchmark performance competitive with or above larger models on selected evaluations. These results are claims in the paper, not independently demonstrated here. In one scientist-guided computational-chemistry workflow, the paper reports ~12 hours of agent execution versus an estimated human work-week; the human estimate is not a measured matched comparison.
technical.demonstrated_result: The arXiv paper is dated 2026-10-20 and the linked model card exposes a 35B MoE model under Apache-2.0. The paper reports author-run ablation scores of 81.7 to 82.8 on BrowseComp and 43.7 to 47.5 on DeepResearch-Bench II with orchestration enabled. The broader table is mixed. The model card links to a GitHub repository for the earlier Agents-A1 model; an A1.5-specific code and evaluation implementation was not identified there. The paper describes author-selected case studies; one scientist-guided chemistry workflow is reported at ~12 hours, against an estimated human work-week, with no matched labor measurement. The paper’s local-deployment figure describes quantized variants as 35B total and 3B active parameters; the report provides no hardware-matched throughput or cost result.
technical.mechanism: Sage-A1.5 is trained to decide when and how to split work across parallel subagents, assign context, integrate results, inspect evidence and revise its strategy. This makes execution organization and feedback-driven adjustment explicit model capabilities.
technical.regime: 35B-total/3B-active Mixture-of-Experts agent model evaluated in the authors’ search, engineering, science and general-agent benchmark harnesses. The orchestration ablation is reported for BrowseComp and DeepResearch-Bench II. The paper depicts quantized local deployment, but supplies no hardware-matched speed or cost result. The Hugging Face model card lists Apache-2.0 weights.
technical.strongest_baseline: The paper’s own Sage-A1.5 no-orchestration condition is the relevant ablation baseline. For this condition the authors report 81.7 BrowseComp and 43.7 DeepResearch-Bench II versus 82.8 and 47.5 with orchestration. No independent matched reproduction or end-to-end cost comparison is available. The model card’s linked GitHub repository is for the earlier Agents-A1; no A1.5-specific evaluation implementation was identified at that destination.

brief.title: Sage-A1.5 tests learned orchestration and verification in a 35B open-weight agent model
brief.why_it_matters: Sage-A1.5 makes orchestration and self-checking explicit targets of model training, rather than leaving all coordination to a fixed external scaffold. If independently reproduced, that approach could change how open models handle long-horizon research and engineering tasks. The paper reports modest, benchmark-specific orchestration gains and mixed broader results; it does not establish a general capability advantage or lower total inference cost. The report also describes a scientist-guided chemistry workflow completed in about 12 hours, compared with the authors’ estimate of a human work-week; this is a single, unmeasured time comparison rather than established productivity gain.
